title: Vietnamese lemongrass chicken
summary: Juicy lemongrass-marinated chicken with garlic, fish sauce and a caramelised, savoury crust.
method: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar and lime juice in a bowl. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 10 minutes.
Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear. Simmer with water per the packet, then rest covered for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in one layer for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and 75°C in the thickest part.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the cucumber and pan juices.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and lime in a bowl.
Coat chicken thoroughly and leave for at least 10 minutes while preparing rice.

stages.title: Cook rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs nearly clear.
Simmer with water according to packet instructions, then rest covered for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Sear chicken
steps: Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and add chicken in one layer.
Cook 5–6 minutes per side until browned and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Rest chicken for 3 minutes before slicing across the grain.
Spoon over rice with cucumber and pan juices.

tips: Wipe excess marinade off before searing to prevent the sugar burning.
variations: Add sliced chilli and fresh mint at serving.
storage: Refrigerate cooked chicken up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Chicken katsu curry
summary: Crispy panko chicken served over rice with a mild, richly spiced Japanese curry sauce.
method: Cook the onion and carrot in a saucepan with a little oil over medium heat until softened. Add the potato and water, then simmer until tender.
Turn off the heat and dissolve the curry roux a little at a time. Return to a gentle simmer until glossy and thick.
Flatten the chicken breasts to 1.5 cm, season, then coat in flour, egg and panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry the chicken in hot oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and 75°C in the centre.
Rest briefly, slice and serve with the rice and curry.

stages.title: Start curry base
steps: Cook onion and carrot in a saucepan with a little oil over medium heat until softened.
Add potato and water; simmer until the vegetables are tender.

stages.title: Finish curry
steps: Turn off the heat and dissolve curry roux blocks a little at a time.
Return to a gentle simmer, stirring until glossy and thick.

stages.title: Crumb chicken
steps: Flatten breasts to even 1.5 cm thickness and season.
Coat in flour, beaten egg and panko, pressing crumbs firmly into the meat.

stages.title: Cook cutlets
steps: Shallow-fry in hot oil over medium heat until golden on both sides.
Check the centre reaches 75°C, rest briefly and slice; serve with rice and curry.

tips: Keep the curry at a gentle simmer after adding roux so it does not catch.
variations: Replace chicken with breaded aubergine and use vegetable curry roux.
storage: Refrigerate curry and chicken separately up to 3 days; re-crisp chicken in oven.

title: Kuku sabzi (herb frittata)
summary: A fragrant Persian herb omelette packed with parsley, coriander, dill and spring onions.
method: Wash and thoroughly dry the parsley, coriander and dill, then chop finely. Combine with the spring onions, walnuts, turmeric, flour and salt.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl, then fold in the herb mixture until every leaf is coated.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick, oven-safe frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the mixture, flatten gently and cook covered until the edges are set.
Transfer the pan to a 180°C oven until the centre is set and lightly browned.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.

stages.title: Prepare herbs
steps: Wash herbs and dry them very thoroughly before chopping finely.
Combine herbs, spring onions, walnuts, turmeric, flour and salt.

stages.title: Mix eggs
steps: Beat eggs in a large bowl until uniform.
Fold herb mixture through until every leaf is coated.

stages.title: Cook first side
steps: Heat oil in a non-stick oven-safe frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add mixture, flatten gently and cook covered until edges are set.

stages.title: Finish and rest
steps: Transfer pan to a 180°C oven until centre is set and lightly browned.
Rest 5 minutes before cutting into wedges.

tips: Dry herbs well to prevent a watery centre.
variations: Add a handful of chopped spinach or dried barberries.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; serve cool or reheat gently.

title: Pozole verde
summary: Hearty Mexican hominy soup with shredded chicken, tangy green chilli broth and crisp toppings.
method: Simmer the chicken in the stock with half the onion over medium heat for about 20 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Shred it and keep the broth.
Grill the tomatillos, jalapeño and remaining onion on high until blistered, then blend with the garlic, coriander stems and a ladle of broth.
Simmer the green sauce in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the broth, hominy, oregano and shredded chicken and simmer for 10 minutes, until heated through.
Season with salt and lime juice. Serve topped with the cabbage, coriander leaves and extra lime.

stages.title: Poach chicken
steps: Simmer chicken in stock with half the onion until cooked through to 75°C.
Remove chicken, cool slightly and shred; reserve the broth.

stages.title: Roast green vegetables
steps: Grill tomatillos, jalapeño and remaining onion until blistered.
Blend with garlic, coriander stems and a ladle of broth.

stages.title: Build soup
steps: Pour green sauce into a large pot and simmer 5 minutes.
Add broth, hominy, oregano and shredded chicken; simmer for 10 minutes until heated through.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Season with salt and lime juice just before serving.
Top with cabbage, coriander leaves and extra lime.

tips: Add lime at the end to keep the green flavour fresh.
variations: Use cooked pork shoulder instead of chicken.
storage: Refrigerate soup up to 3 days; keep crunchy toppings separate.

title: Seafood paella
summary: Saffron rice studded with seafood, peppers and peas, cooked until a crisp socarrat forms underneath.
method: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat and soften the capsicum for about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, grated tomatoes and smoked paprika. Cook for about 7 minutes, until reduced to a thick paste.
Stir in the bomba rice to coat it, then add the hot fish stock with the saffron and spread the rice evenly.
Simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, adjusting the heat to keep a gentle bubble. Arrange the prawns and mussels on top.
Cook for another 8–10 minutes, until the prawns are opaque and the mussels have opened. Discard any that stay closed, rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

stages.title: Prepare sofrito
steps: Heat oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat and soften capsicum for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Add garlic, grated tomato and paprika; cook until reduced to a thick paste.

stages.title: Toast rice
steps: Stir in rice so each grain is coated in the sofrito.
Add saffron-infused hot stock and distribute rice evenly across the pan.

stages.title: Cook undisturbed
steps: Simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain a gentle bubbling surface.
Arrange prawns and mussels on top and cook for the final 8–10 minutes, until prawns are opaque and mussels have opened.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check prawns are opaque and mussels have opened; discard any that remain closed.
Rest paella covered loosely for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

tips: Avoid stirring after adding stock so the rice can form a crisp base.
variations: Use squid rings or firm white fish in place of some prawns.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 2 days; reheat seafood thoroughly once.

title: Ratatouille
summary: Slow-cooked aubergine, courgette, peppers and tomatoes infused with garlic and Provençal herbs.
method: Sprinkle the aubergine with salt, leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat most of the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown the aubergine, courgettes and capsicums in batches until lightly golden, then set aside.
Lower to medium heat. Soften the onion and garlic in the remaining oil for about 5 minutes, without browning.
Add the tomatoes and thyme and simmer until juicy and starting to break down.
Return the vegetables to the pan and simmer gently until tender but not mushy.
Stir in the vinegar, season with salt and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

stages.title: Salt aubergine
steps: Sprinkle diced aubergine with a little salt and leave briefly.
Pat dry to remove surface moisture.

stages.title: Brown vegetables
steps: Cook aubergine in batches with oil over medium-high heat until lightly golden; transfer to a bowl.
Repeat with courgettes and capsicums so they retain some texture.

stages.title: Build tomato base
steps: Soften onion and garlic in remaining oil for about 5 minutes without browning.
Add tomatoes and thyme; simmer until juicy and beginning to break down.

stages.title: Finish stew
steps: Return vegetables to the pan and simmer gently until tender but not mushy.
Add vinegar, season and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

tips: Cooking vegetables separately helps them retain distinct flavours.
variations: Top with fresh basil just before serving.
storage: Refrigerate 4 days; freezes well for 2 months.

title: Kimchi fried rice
summary: Day-old rice stir-fried with tangy kimchi, sesame oil and a golden fried egg.
method: Break up the chilled rice and chop the kimchi. Mix the gochujang, kimchi juice and soy sauce into a sauce.
Heat the neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the kimchi for about 4 minutes, until the edges caramelise and the pan looks less wet.
Add the rice and sauce, tossing to coat. Press the rice against the pan for a few minutes, until crisp in spots.
Stir through the sesame oil and sliced spring onions until heated through.
Fry the eggs separately until the whites are fully set and the yolks are done how you like them. Top the rice with the eggs and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Break up chilled rice with clean hands or a fork so there are no large clumps.
Chop kimchi and mix gochujang with kimchi juice and soy sauce.

stages.title: Fry kimchi
steps: Heat neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook kimchi until its edges start to caramelise and the pan looks less wet.

stages.title: Fry rice
steps: Add rice and toss with kimchi sauce, pressing it against the pan briefly to crisp.
Stir through sesame oil and sliced spring onions.

stages.title: Finish with eggs
steps: Fry eggs separately until whites are fully set and yolks reach your preferred doneness.
Top rice with eggs and sesame seeds.

tips: Use rice chilled promptly after cooking and stored in the fridge; do not leave cooked rice out overnight.
variations: Add diced spam or cooked tofu for extra protein.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 1 day and reheat thoroughly only once.

title: Palak paneer
summary: Soft paneer cubes in a velvety spinach curry scented with garlic, ginger and garam masala.
method: Wilt the spinach in boiling water, then cool in cold water. Drain well and blend with a splash of water until smooth.
Heat the ghee in a pan over medium heat. Sizzle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, chilli, tomatoes and turmeric. Cook until thick.
Stir in the spinach purée and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Add the garam masala and cream, loosening with a little water if needed.
Add the paneer and heat gently for 3–4 minutes until warmed through. Season, and serve with roti or rice if using.

stages.title: Blanch spinach
steps: Wilt spinach briefly in boiling water, then transfer to cold water.
Drain thoroughly and blend with a splash of water until smooth.

stages.title: Make masala
steps: Heat ghee and sizzle cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Cook onion over medium heat until golden, then add ginger, garlic, chilli, tomatoes and turmeric until thick.

stages.title: Combine sauce
steps: Stir spinach purée into masala and simmer gently for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add garam masala and cream, loosening with water if needed.

stages.title: Warm paneer
steps: Add paneer cubes and heat gently until warmed through.
Season and serve with roti or rice; avoid boiling hard or paneer may toughen.

tips: Avoid overcooking spinach to preserve its bright green colour.
variations: Use firm tofu and coconut cream for a dairy-free version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently.

title: Harira
summary: Warming Moroccan tomato soup with lentils, chickpeas, herbs and fragrant spices.
method: Soften the onion and celery in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat for about 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the ginger, turmeric and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Add the grated tomatoes, lentils and stock. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 30 minutes until the lentils are tender, then add the chickpeas.
Break the vermicelli into short lengths and stir in. Simmer for about 7 minutes until just cooked, adding water if the soup gets too thick.
Stir through the chopped coriander and the juice of the lemon. Season to taste and serve with extra lemon wedges.

stages.title: Cook aromatic base
steps: Soften onion and celery in olive oil over medium heat until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add ginger, turmeric and cinnamon, stirring for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Simmer legumes
steps: Add grated tomatoes, lentils and stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook until lentils are tender, then add drained chickpeas.

stages.title: Add noodles
steps: Break vermicelli into short lengths and stir into soup.
Simmer until the vermicelli is just cooked, adding water if soup thickens too much.

stages.title: Finish fresh
steps: Stir through chopped coriander and lemon juice.
Taste and season, then serve with extra lemon wedges.

tips: Add noodles near the end so they do not turn mushy.
variations: Add diced cooked lamb for a heartier version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze without noodles for best texture.

title: Misir wot
summary: Tender red lentils simmered in a deeply spiced Ethiopian berbere sauce.
method: Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until softened and golden. Add the olive oil once they catch and cook until sweet and reduced.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste. Cook over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant, adding a splash of water if it scorches.
Add the lentils and water. Simmer gently for about 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils break down into a thick stew.
Loosen with a little hot water if the stew gets too stiff. Season with the salt.
Serve with rice or injera.

stages.title: Cook onions slowly
steps: Cook onions in a dry heavy pot over medium-low heat, stirring often until softened and golden.
Add oil once they begin to catch, then continue until sweet and reduced.

stages.title: Bloom spices
steps: Stir in garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste.
Cook briefly over low heat until fragrant, adding a splash of water to prevent scorching.

stages.title: Simmer lentils
steps: Add rinsed lentils and water, stirring well to release the spiced onion base.
Simmer gently, stirring frequently, until lentils break down into a thick stew.

stages.title: Adjust texture
steps: Add hot water a little at a time if the stew becomes too stiff.
Season and serve with injera or rice.

tips: Berbere blends vary in heat; start with less and adjust.
variations: Add diced carrots for a sweeter version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze up to 3 months.

title: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
summary: Pillowy potato gnocchi baked with tomato, basil and melted mozzarella until bubbling.
method: Warm the oil and garlic in a saucepan over low heat for about 1 minute until fragrant, without browning.
Add the passata and salt and simmer over medium heat for about 10 minutes until slightly thickened, then stir through the torn basil.
Boil the gnocchi in batches in gently boiling salted water, lifting each batch out with a slotted spoon as soon as it floats, about 2 minutes.
Toss the gnocchi with the sauce in an ovenproof dish, then dot with the mozzarella and sprinkle over the Parmesan.
Bake at 220°C for about 10 minutes until the cheese bubbles and lightly browns, then rest for 3 minutes before serving.

stages.title: Cook tomato sauce
steps: Warm oil and garlic gently in a saucepan without browning.
Add passata and salt, simmer until slightly thickened and stir in torn basil.

stages.title: Boil gnocchi
steps: Bring salted water to a gentle boil and add gnocchi in batches.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.

stages.title: Assemble bake
steps: Toss drained gnocchi with tomato sauce in an ovenproof dish.
Dot with mozzarella and sprinkle Parmesan evenly over the surface.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake at 220°C until cheese bubbles and lightly browns.
Rest for 3 minutes before serving so the sauce clings to the gnocchi.

tips: Drain mozzarella well to prevent a watery bake.
variations: Add sautéed aubergine for extra vegetables.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat covered until hot.

title: Piri piri chicken
summary: Juicy chicken marinated in fiery piri piri, lemon and garlic, roasted until charred at the edges.
method: Blend the chillies, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, oregano, oil and salt into a marinade. Taste and adjust the heat.
Pat the chicken dry and score the thick parts. Coat in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if time allows.
Arrange the chicken skin-side up on a rack over a tray. Roast at 200°C for about 35 minutes, turning the tray halfway, until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes so the juices settle.
Serve with lemon wedges and roasted potatoes, if using.

stages.title: Blend marinade
steps: Blend chillies, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, oregano, oil and salt.
Taste the marinade before it touches raw chicken and adjust heat.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Pat chicken dry and score thick sections lightly.
Coat evenly with marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if time allows.

stages.title: Roast chicken
steps: Arrange pieces skin-side up on a rack over a tray and roast at 200°C.
Turn tray halfway and cook until thickest part of each piece reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest chicken 5–10 minutes so juices settle.
Serve with lemon wedges and roasted potatoes.

tips: Keep a separate portion of marinade for serving; never reuse raw-chicken marinade without boiling it.
variations: Use boneless thighs and shorten cooking time, checking temperature.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze cooked chicken up to 2 months.

title: Turkey chilli
summary: Hearty turkey chilli with beans, tomatoes, peppers and smoky spices.
method: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and capsicum for about 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the turkey mince, breaking it up, and cook until no pink remains and most of the liquid has evaporated, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and spices (cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder) and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock. Simmer uncovered for about 25 minutes until thick and rich.
Season with salt and adjust the chilli heat, then rest for 5 minutes. Serve with rice or yoghurt if you like.

stages.title: Soften vegetables
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook onion and capsicum for about 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Brown turkey
steps: Add turkey mince and break it into small pieces.
Cook until no pink remains and excess liquid has mostly evaporated.

stages.title: Build chilli
steps: Stir in tomato paste and spices, cooking 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, beans and stock; simmer uncovered until thick and rich.

stages.title: Finish
steps: Taste and adjust salt and chilli heat.
Rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or yoghurt.

tips: A little resting time makes the chilli thicker and more cohesive.
variations: Swap kidney beans for black beans or add sweetcorn.
storage: Refrigerate 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Lomo saltado
summary: Stir-fried beef, tomatoes and onions tossed with chips in a punchy soy-vinegar sauce.
method: Bake the oven chips at 220°C according to the packet, until crisp. Slice the sirloin across the grain and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until very hot. Sear the steak in batches, about 1 minute per side, until browned. Remove.
Stir-fry the red onion wedges in the wok until charred at the edges but still crisp. Add the garlic and tomato wedges and toss for 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the soy sauce, red wine vinegar and cumin. Toss for about 1 minute, until coated and cooked to your liking.
Serve straight away with the chips, rice and coriander.

stages.title: Prepare components
steps: Bake oven chips at 220°C according to packet instructions until crisp.
Slice steak across the grain and pat dry for good browning.

stages.title: Sear beef
steps: Heat a wok or large pan over high heat until very hot, then add oil.
Sear steak quickly in batches, about 1 minute per side until browned, so it browns rather than steams; remove.

stages.title: Stir-fry vegetables
steps: Add onion wedges and cook until charred at edges but still crisp.
Add garlic and tomato wedges and toss briefly for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Return beef with soy sauce, vinegar and cumin, tossing for about 1 minute until coated and cooked to preference.
Serve immediately with chips, rice and coriander.

tips: High heat and small batches give the characteristic smoky sear.
variations: Use chicken strips instead of beef, cooking through to 75°C.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days; chips are best fresh.

title: Cajun shrimp and grits
summary: Creamy stone-ground grits topped with juicy Cajun-spiced prawns and a buttery pan sauce.
method: Simmer the stock and milk over medium heat, whisk in the grits and cook until thick and creamy, about 10 minutes. Stir in the cheddar.
Pat the prawns dry and toss with the Cajun seasoning. Chop the capsicum, garlic and spring onions.
Heat the butter and oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the capsicum for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink, opaque and firm.
Loosen the grits with a little warm water if needed and spoon into bowls. Top with the prawns, pan juices and sliced spring onions.

stages.title: Cook grits
steps: Bring stock and milk to a simmer and whisk in grits gradually.
Cook according to packet, stirring frequently until creamy; stir in cheddar.

stages.title: Prepare prawns
steps: Pat prawns dry and toss with Cajun seasoning.
Chop capsicum, garlic and spring onions while grits cook.

stages.title: Sauté topping
steps: Heat butter and oil in a pan over medium-high heat and soften capsicum for 3 minutes.
Add garlic and prawns; cook for 2 to 3 minutes until prawns turn pink, opaque and firm.

stages.title: Serve immediately
steps: Loosen grits with warm water if needed and spoon into bowls.
Top with prawns, pan juices and sliced spring onions.

tips: Season grits gradually because stock and cheese already contain salt.
variations: Use polenta if grits are unavailable, following its longer cooking time.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat grits with extra liquid.

title: Brazilian black bean stew
summary: Slow-simmered black beans with vegetables, garlic and spices for a hearty Brazilian-style stew.
method: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned on both sides, then remove it.
Cook the onion in the pot over medium heat until soft and lightly golden. Add the garlic, cumin and bay leaves and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, stock and sausage and bring to a gentle simmer for about 35 minutes. Mash a spoonful of beans against the pot to thicken the stew.
Simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes, until thick but still spoonable.
Remove the bay leaves. Serve with the rice and orange wedges.

stages.title: Brown sausage
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown sliced sausage on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes, until deeply browned.
Remove sausage, leaving a little flavoured oil in the pot.

stages.title: Build aromatics
steps: Cook onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add garlic, cumin and bay leaves and stir for 1 minute.

stages.title: Simmer beans
steps: Add beans, stock and sausage; bring to a gentle simmer.
Mash a spoonful of beans against the pot to thicken the liquid naturally.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Simmer uncovered until stew is thick but still spoonable.
Remove bay leaves and serve with rice and orange wedges.

tips: Smashing some beans gives a creamy broth without flour.
variations: Use roasted mushrooms instead of sausage for a meat-free version.
storage: Refrigerate 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Thai basil chicken (pad krapow)
summary: Minced chicken flash-fried with garlic, chilli and holy basil, served over rice.
ingredients: 1 handful Thai holy basil or Thai basil
method: Rinse the jasmine rice and cook on low heat per the packet until tender. Keep covered and warm.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together. Finely chop the garlic and chillies.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic and chilli briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken mince, breaking it up, and cook until cooked through (75°C), about 6 minutes.
Add the sauce and toss until it coats the meat and reduces slightly.
Turn off the heat, fold in the basil and serve over the rice.

stages.title: Cook rice
steps: Rinse rice and cook according to packet instructions, on low heat once boiling, until tender.
Keep covered and warm while preparing the stir-fry.

stages.title: Mix sauce
steps: Stir oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together.
Chop garlic and chilli finely so they release flavour quickly.

stages.title: Stir-fry chicken
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and briefly fry garlic and chilli.
Add chicken mince, breaking it up and cooking until fully cooked through to 75°C.

stages.title: Finish with basil
steps: Add sauce and toss until it coats the meat and reduces slightly.
Turn off heat, fold in basil and serve over rice.

tips: Holy basil gives the most traditional peppery aroma.
variations: Use minced pork or crumbled firm tofu instead.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Arancini
summary: Crisp golden rice balls filled with savoury risotto and melting cheese.
method: Chill the cooked risotto rice until firm. Cube the mozzarella and simmer the passata until thick, so the filling won't leak.
With damp hands, flatten a portion of rice, add a mozzarella cube and a teaspoon of passata, then seal into a ball.
Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Press crumbs over any cracks and chill briefly if soft.
Heat the oil to 170–175°C and fry in batches until golden and piping hot inside.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with the Parmesan before serving.

stages.title: Prepare filling
steps: Chill risotto thoroughly so it is firm enough to shape.
Cut mozzarella into small cubes and keep the passata thick to prevent leaking.

stages.title: Shape balls
steps: With damp hands flatten a portion of rice in your palm.
Add a cube of mozzarella and a teaspoon of sauce, then seal tightly into a ball.

stages.title: Bread evenly
steps: Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Press crumbs onto any cracks and chill briefly if soft.

stages.title: Fry and drain
steps: Heat oil to 170–175°C and fry in batches until golden and piping hot inside.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with Parmesan before serving.

tips: Cold, thick risotto makes shaping much easier.
variations: Fill with cooked mushrooms and peas instead of tomato sauce.
storage: Refrigerate cooked arancini up to 2 days; reheat in oven.

title: Miso aubergine (nasu dengaku)
summary: Roasted aubergine glazed with sweet-savoury miso, mirin and sesame until tender and caramelised.
method: Halve the aubergines lengthways, score the flesh in a shallow crosshatch without cutting the skin, then brush the cut sides with oil and place on a baking tray.
Roast cut-side up at 210°C for about 20 minutes, until the flesh is golden and a spoon presses in with no resistance.
Whisk the miso, mirin, sugar and sake (or water) until smooth. Warm in a small pan over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Spread the glaze over the aubergine and grill for about 4 minutes, until bubbling and caramelised.
Scatter the sesame seeds and sliced spring onions over the top.

stages.title: Score aubergine
steps: Halve aubergines lengthways and score flesh in a shallow crosshatch without cutting skin.
Brush cut sides with oil and place on a baking tray.

stages.title: Roast until soft
steps: Roast cut-side up at 210°C until flesh is tender and golden.
Test with a spoon; it should give easily without resistance.

stages.title: Make miso glaze
steps: Whisk miso, mirin, sugar and sake until smooth.
Warm gently in a small pan just until sugar dissolves.

stages.title: Glaze and grill
steps: Spread glaze over aubergine and grill briefly until bubbling and caramelised.
Scatter sesame seeds and spring onions over top.

tips: Watch closely under the grill because miso glaze burns quickly.
variations: Use red miso for a stronger savoury flavour, reducing the quantity slightly.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in oven.

title: Aloo gobi
summary: Cauliflower and potatoes cooked with turmeric, cumin, ginger and fragrant Indian spices.
method: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sizzle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. Add the potatoes and cook until the edges start to colour.
Add the onion, ginger and garlic and cook until softened. Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander briefly.
Add the cauliflower, tomatoes and a splash of water. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the potatoes and cauliflower are tender, about 15 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for about 5 minutes, until the moisture has cooked off and the spices cling to the vegetables. Season and finish with the coriander leaves.

stages.title: Start potatoes
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sizzle cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add potatoes and cook over medium heat until edges begin to colour.

stages.title: Add aromatics
steps: Stir in onion, ginger and garlic and cook until softened.
Add turmeric and ground coriander, stirring briefly.

stages.title: Cook cauliflower
steps: Add cauliflower, tomatoes and a splash of water.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently, until potatoes and cauliflower are tender.

stages.title: Dry and finish
steps: Remove lid and cook off excess moisture for about 5 minutes, until the spices cling to vegetables.
Season and finish with fresh coriander.

tips: Cut potato smaller than cauliflower so both finish together.
variations: Add peas in the final 5 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat in a pan.

title: Mediterranean stuffed peppers
summary: Sweet peppers filled with herbed rice, vegetables and savoury tomato sauce, then baked until tender.
method: Halve the capsicums lengthways, keeping the stems, and remove the seeds. Brush with olive oil and place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat and soften the onion in oil for about 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes and oregano.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the tomatoes lose their excess moisture, then fold in the rice, olives and lemon zest. Let cool.
Stir the parsley and half the feta through the filling, then pack into the capsicums and top with the remaining feta.
Add a splash of water to the dish and cover loosely with foil. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake for about 15 minutes more, until the capsicums are tender and the tops are lightly golden.

stages.title: Prepare peppers
steps: Halve capsicums lengthways and remove seeds while keeping stems intact.
Brush with oil and place cut-side up in a baking dish.

stages.title: Cook filling
steps: Soften onion in a frying pan with oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes until translucent, then add tomatoes and oregano.
Cook until tomatoes lose excess moisture and fold in rice, olives and lemon zest.

stages.title: Fill peppers
steps: Stir parsley and half the feta through the cooled filling.
Pack mixture into pepper halves and sprinkle with remaining feta.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Add a splash of water to the dish and cover loosely with foil for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake until peppers are tender and tops lightly golden.

tips: Use already cooked rice for a reliable baking time.
variations: Add cooked lentils or chickpeas for extra protein.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Bánh mì
summary: Crusty Vietnamese baguette stuffed with savoury fillings, pickled vegetables, cucumber and fresh coriander.
method: Toss the carrot and daikon with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Leave to soften for about 10 minutes, then drain lightly.
Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce and garlic, then coat the pork slices. Leave to stand briefly while the pan heats.
Sear the pork in batches in an oiled frying pan over high heat until browned and cooked through to 63°C. Rest for 3 minutes.
Reduce any remaining clean marinade separately until slightly thickened, then spoon it over the pork.
Warm the baguettes until crusty, then split and spread with the mayonnaise. Layer the cucumber, pork, pickles and coriander, and serve immediately.

stages.title: Quick-pickle vegetables
steps: Toss carrot and daikon with vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Leave to soften while preparing the pork, then drain lightly.

stages.title: Season pork
steps: Mix soy sauce, fish sauce and garlic and coat pork slices.
Allow to stand briefly while heating the pan.

stages.title: Cook pork
steps: Sear pork in a hot oiled frying pan in batches until browned and cooked through to 63°C, then rest 3 minutes.
Reduce any remaining clean marinade separately before spooning over pork.

stages.title: Build sandwiches
steps: Warm baguettes until crusty, then split and spread with mayonnaise.
Layer cucumber, pork, drained pickles and coriander; serve immediately.

tips: Use light, crisp baguettes rather than dense sourdough.
variations: Substitute cooked tofu and soy sauce for pork and fish sauce.
storage: Keep fillings refrigerated separately up to 2 days; assemble fresh.

title: Minestrone
summary: Rustic Italian vegetable soup with beans, pasta and tomatoes in a deeply savoury broth.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for about 10 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock and courgette and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for about 20 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Stir in the cannellini beans and pasta. Simmer for about 10 minutes until the pasta is al dente, adding water if the soup gets too thick.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

stages.title: Sweat vegetables
steps: Heat oil and cook onion, carrot and celery over medium-low heat until softened.
Add garlic and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

stages.title: Build soup
steps: Add tomatoes, stock and courgette, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook until vegetables are nearly tender.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Stir in drained beans and pasta.
Simmer until pasta is al dente, adding water if the soup thickens too much.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

tips: Cook pasta separately if planning leftovers so it doesn't absorb all the broth.
variations: Add kale or spinach in the last few minutes.
storage: Refrigerate 4 days; freeze best without pasta.

title: Cobb salad
summary: A hearty chopped salad with chicken, avocado, bacon, egg, tomato and tangy dressing.
method: Cook the chicken in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until the centre reaches 75°C, then rest and dice.
Cook the bacon until crisp. Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool and quarter.
Chop the cos lettuce, and dice the tomatoes and avocado just before assembling.
Whisk the vinegar, Dijon mustard and olive oil until emulsified, then season lightly with salt.
Spread the lettuce on a platter and arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, tomatoes and avocado in rows. Crumble over the blue cheese and drizzle with dressing at serving.

stages.title: Cook proteins
steps: Cook chicken in a lightly oiled pan until centre reaches 75°C, then rest and dice.
Cook bacon until crisp and hard-boil eggs for 10 minutes, then cool and quarter.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Wash and dry lettuce thoroughly and chop into bite-size pieces.
Dice tomatoes and avocado just before assembling.

stages.title: Whisk dressing
steps: Whisk vinegar, mustard and olive oil until emulsified.
Season lightly, remembering bacon and cheese add salt.

stages.title: Arrange salad
steps: Spread lettuce over a platter and arrange chicken, bacon, eggs, tomatoes and avocado in rows.
Crumble blue cheese over and drizzle dressing at serving.

tips: Dry lettuce well so the dressing adheres.
variations: Use feta instead of blue cheese.
storage: Refrigerate undressed components up to 2 days; add avocado fresh.

title: Menemen
summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes, green peppers and Turkish spices, served with bread.
method: Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and green peppers for about 6 minutes, until tender.
Add the grated tomatoes, paprika and salt. Simmer uncovered for about 7 minutes, until the liquid evaporates and the sauce thickens.
Lightly beat the eggs and pour them in. Cook over low heat for about 4 minutes, until softly set and still moist.
Take the pan off the heat before the eggs dry out. Scatter over the parsley and serve with the crusty bread for scooping.

stages.title: Soften peppers
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat and cook onion and peppers until tender.
Avoid high heat so the vegetables sweeten rather than scorch.

stages.title: Reduce tomatoes
steps: Add grated tomatoes, paprika and salt.
Simmer uncovered until excess liquid evaporates and sauce thickens.

stages.title: Add eggs
steps: Beat eggs lightly and pour into tomato mixture.
Stir slowly over low heat until softly set and still moist.

stages.title: Serve hot
steps: Remove pan from heat before eggs become dry.
Sprinkle parsley over and serve with bread for scooping.

tips: Eggs continue cooking in the hot pan, so stop while slightly loose.
variations: Add crumbled feta just before serving.
storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers up to 1 day and reheat thoroughly.

title: Porridge with stewed pears
summary: Creamy slow-cooked oats topped with tender cinnamon pears and a drizzle of honey.
method: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Cook the pears and cinnamon until soft but holding their shape, then stir in the honey.
Combine the oats, milk, water and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often.
Reduce to low and simmer until the oats are tender and the porridge thickens. Add a splash more milk if it gets too stiff.
Divide the porridge into bowls, spoon the warm pears over and scatter with the walnuts.

stages.title: Stew pears
steps: Melt butter in a small pan and add diced pears and cinnamon.
Cook over medium-low heat until soft but holding shape, then stir in honey.

stages.title: Start porridge
steps: Combine oats, milk, water and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.

stages.title: Cook until creamy
steps: Continue simmering on low heat until oats are tender and porridge thickens.
Add a splash more milk if it becomes too stiff.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide porridge into bowls and spoon warm pears over top.
Scatter walnuts over just before eating for crunch.

tips: A pinch of salt makes oats taste sweeter without extra sugar.
variations: Replace pears with apples or use oat milk.
storage: Refrigerate plain porridge up to 3 days; reheat with extra milk.

title: Huevos rancheros
summary: Fried eggs on crisp tortillas with smoky beans, tomato salsa and fresh coriander.
method: Soften the onion, garlic and jalapeño in a little oil in a pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until soft. Add the tomatoes and cumin and simmer until thick enough to spoon.
Warm the beans with a splash of water and a pinch of salt over medium heat until hot. Mash a small portion for a creamy texture.
Fry the eggs in oil in a non-stick pan until the whites are fully set. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until pliable.
Spread the beans on the tortillas and add a spoonful of salsa. Top with the eggs, sliced avocado and a squeeze of lime juice.

stages.title: Cook salsa
steps: Soften onion, garlic and jalapeño in a little oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Add tomatoes and cumin and simmer until thick enough to spoon.

stages.title: Warm beans
steps: Heat drained beans with a splash of water and pinch of salt.
Mash a small portion to create a creamy texture.

stages.title: Cook eggs
steps: Heat oil in a non-stick pan and fry eggs until whites are fully set.
Warm tortillas separately in a dry pan until pliable.

stages.title: Assemble plates
steps: Spread beans on tortillas and add a spoonful of salsa.
Top with eggs, avocado slices and lime juice.

tips: Keep salsa fairly thick so tortillas do not become soggy.
variations: Add crumbled feta or fresh coriander.
storage: Refrigerate salsa and beans separately up to 3 days; eggs best fresh.

title: Croque monsieur
summary: Toasted ham and cheese sandwich with creamy béchamel and a golden Gruyère crust.
method: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until smooth and thick, then season with the nutmeg.
Spread the sourdough with Dijon mustard, then layer on the ham and half the Gruyère. Close into sandwiches and place on a lined baking tray.
Spoon the béchamel over each sandwich and scatter on the remaining Gruyère.
Bake at 220°C until the bread is crisp and the topping bubbles and browns.
Rest for 2 minutes before cutting, then serve hot with a sharp green salad.

stages.title: Make béchamel
steps: Melt butter over medium heat, stir in flour and cook 1 minute without browning.
Whisk in milk gradually and simmer until smooth and thick; season with nutmeg.

stages.title: Build sandwiches
steps: Spread bread with mustard and layer ham and half the cheese.
Close sandwiches and place on a lined baking tray.

stages.title: Top and bake
steps: Spoon béchamel over each sandwich and scatter remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 220°C until bread is crisp and topping bubbles and browns.

stages.title: Rest briefly
steps: Let sandwiches stand for 2 minutes before cutting.
Serve hot with a sharp green salad.

tips: Use a thick béchamel so it stays on top rather than soaking bread.
variations: Top each with a fried egg for croque madame.
storage: Best fresh; refrigerate assembled unbaked sandwiches up to 1 day.

title: Congee with ginger
summary: Comforting rice porridge simmered until silky, finished with ginger, spring onion and savoury toppings.
method: Rinse the jasmine rice and drain. Put it in a heavy saucepan with the stock and sliced ginger.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to low for a very gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered for about 50 minutes, until the rice starts to break down, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick.
Keep cooking for about 10 minutes, until the congee is thick and silky. Loosen with hot water if needed, then season with the soy sauce and white pepper.
Remove the large ginger slices and ladle the congee into bowls.
Top with sliced eggs, spring onions and a few drops of sesame oil.

stages.title: Rinse rice
steps: Rinse rice briefly and drain.
Place in a heavy saucepan with stock and sliced ginger.

stages.title: Simmer gently
steps: Bring to a boil, then lower to a very gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for about 50 minutes, until the rice begins to break down, stirring occasionally so rice does not stick to the base.

stages.title: Adjust texture
steps: Continue cooking until grains break down and porridge is thick and silky.
Add hot water to loosen if needed, then season with soy sauce and white pepper.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Remove large ginger slices and ladle congee into bowls.
Top with sliced eggs, spring onions and a few drops of sesame oil.

tips: Stir more frequently as the congee thickens.
variations: Top with shredded cooked chicken or sautéed mushrooms.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 3 days; reheat with water until piping hot.

title: Smashed avocado toast
summary: Crunchy sourdough topped with smashed avocado, lemon, chilli and fresh herbs.
method: Toast the sourdough until crisp and golden on the outside, then place on plates while still warm.
Mash the avocado roughly with the lemon juice and salt, keeping some chunks for texture.
Spread the avocado over the toast, then scatter over the feta, chilli flakes and mint.
Drizzle with the olive oil and serve straight away.

stages.title: Toast bread
steps: Toast sourdough until crisp and golden on the outside.
Place on plates while still warm.

stages.title: Mash avocado
steps: Scoop avocado into a bowl and mash roughly with lemon juice and salt.
Keep some chunks for texture rather than making a smooth purée.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Spread avocado generously over toast.
Scatter feta, chilli flakes and chopped mint on top.

stages.title: Finish
steps: Drizzle with olive oil and serve immediately.
Add extra lemon if desired to balance the richness.

tips: Ripe but firm avocado gives the best texture.
variations: Add a poached egg or sliced tomatoes.
storage: Best fresh; avocado browns quickly after mashing.

title: Poha with peanuts
summary: Fluffy flattened rice tossed with turmeric, curry leaves, peanuts and fresh lemon.
method: Rinse the poha in a sieve until just damp, then leave it to soften so the grains stay separate.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves carefully.
Add the potato and cook covered for about 8 minutes, until tender.
Add the onion and green chilli and cook until soft. Stir in the turmeric and peanuts for 30 seconds.
Fold the poha through gently and warm until steaming. Season with salt, lemon juice and coriander.

stages.title: Rinse poha
steps: Rinse poha briefly in a sieve until just damp, then leave to soften.
Check grains remain separate and are not waterlogged.

stages.title: Cook potato
steps: Heat oil over medium heat, pop mustard seeds and add curry leaves carefully.
Add diced potato and cook covered over medium heat until tender, stirring occasionally.

stages.title: Add aromatics
steps: Add onion and chilli and cook until soft.
Stir in turmeric and peanuts for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Finish poha
steps: Fold softened poha through gently and warm until steaming.
Season with salt, lemon juice and coriander.

tips: Thick poha holds its shape better than thin flakes.
variations: Add peas for colour and sweetness.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat until hot.

title: Blueberry muffins
summary: Soft blueberry muffins with tender crumb, juicy berries and lightly golden tops.
method: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a 12-hole muffin tray. Toss the blueberries with the extra tablespoon of flour.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in one bowl. In another, whisk the eggs, milk, cooled melted butter and vanilla.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry until no dry flour remains, then gently fold in the blueberries. A few lumps are fine.
Divide the batter among the cases and bake until risen and a skewer comes out without wet batter.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

stages.title: Prepare tins
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a 12-hole muffin tray.
Toss blueberries with a tablespoon of flour to reduce sinking.

stages.title: Mix dry and wet
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in one bowl.
In another, whisk eggs, milk, melted cooled butter and vanilla.

stages.title: Combine batter
steps: Fold wet mixture into dry just until no dry flour remains.
Gently fold in blueberries; a few lumps are desirable.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Divide batter among cases and bake until risen and a skewer comes out without wet batter.
Cool in tin 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

tips: Overmixing develops gluten and makes muffins tough.
variations: Replace blueberries with raspberries or chopped apple.
storage: Airtight at room temperature 2 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Affogato
summary: Hot espresso poured over cold vanilla ice cream for a simple bittersweet Italian dessert.
method: Chill two serving glasses in the freezer for about 2 minutes, then scoop the vanilla gelato into them.
Brew two fresh espresso shots just before serving, so the coffee is piping hot.
Pour one hot espresso shot over the gelato in each glass.
Top with the grated dark chocolate and crushed amaretti biscuits, then serve straight away with spoons before the gelato melts completely.

stages.title: Chill glasses
steps: Place serving glasses in the freezer briefly so gelato melts more slowly.
Scoop gelato into the chilled glasses.

stages.title: Brew coffee
steps: Prepare two fresh espresso shots immediately before serving.
Keep coffee hot for the contrast against the frozen gelato.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Pour one hot espresso shot over each serving of gelato.
Sprinkle with grated chocolate and crushed amaretti.

stages.title: Serve immediately
steps: Bring glasses to the table straight away.
Serve with spoons so the melting gelato and coffee can be eaten together.

tips: Strong espresso balances sweet gelato.
variations: Use decaffeinated espresso or hazelnut gelato.
storage: Assemble only when ready to serve; do not store combined.

title: Sticky toffee pudding
summary: Soft date sponge drenched in warm, buttery toffee sauce.
method: Pour the boiling water over the dates and stir in the bicarbonate of soda. Leave until soft, then mash to a coarse paste.
Beat the butter and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, vanilla and date mixture just until combined.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the cream, the sauce brown sugar and the sauce butter in a pan over low heat until dissolved. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until glossy.
Pour the toffee sauce over the warm pudding.

stages.title: Soften dates
steps: Pour boiling water over chopped dates and stir in bicarbonate of soda.
Leave until soft, then mash lightly into a coarse paste.

stages.title: Make batter
steps: Cream butter and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, vanilla and date mixture just until combined.

stages.title: Bake sponge
steps: Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest 5 minutes while making sauce.

stages.title: Make toffee sauce
steps: Heat cream, extra brown sugar and butter gently until dissolved.
Simmer 3–4 minutes until glossy, then pour over warm pudding.

tips: Do not overbake; the date sponge should remain moist.
variations: Add a pinch of sea salt to the sauce.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat portions with sauce.

title: French chocolate mousse
summary: Airy dark chocolate mousse with a silky texture and intense cocoa flavour.
method: Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water on low heat. Take it off the heat and cool until just warm.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks, not stiff, then refrigerate.
Beat the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then add the sugar gradually. Keep beating until glossy medium peaks form.
Stir the egg yolks and vanilla into the cooled chocolate, then fold in the cream and egg whites in batches.
Divide into glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until set.

stages.title: Melt chocolate
steps: Melt chocolate gently over a pan of barely simmering water.
Remove from heat and cool until just warm, not hot.

stages.title: Whip cream
steps: Whip cold cream to soft peaks and refrigerate briefly.
Avoid stiff peaks, which make folding difficult.

stages.title: Whip egg whites
steps: Beat pasteurised egg whites with salt until foamy, then add sugar gradually.
Continue until glossy medium peaks form.

stages.title: Fold and chill
steps: Stir egg yolks and vanilla into cooled chocolate, then fold in cream and egg whites in batches.
Divide into glasses and refrigerate at least 4 hours before serving.

tips: Use pasteurised eggs because this mousse is not cooked.
variations: Add finely grated orange zest to the chocolate.
storage: Keep refrigerated up to 2 days; do not freeze.

title: New York baked cheesecake
summary: Dense, creamy baked cheesecake with a buttery biscuit base and delicate vanilla tang.
method: Crush the digestive biscuits and mix with the melted butter. Press into a lined springform tin and chill while you make the filling.
Beat the cream cheese and caster sugar until smooth. Mix in the eggs one at a time, then the sour cream, vanilla, lemon zest and cornflour, without overbeating.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake at 160°C until the edges are set but the centre still wobbles slightly.
Turn off the oven and leave the door ajar for 30 minutes to cool gradually.
Cool completely at room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Run a warm knife around the edge, then remove the tin and slice.

stages.title: Make crust
steps: Crush biscuits finely and mix with melted butter.
Press firmly into a lined springform tin and chill while preparing filling.

stages.title: Mix filling
steps: Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, scraping bowl sides.
Mix in eggs one at a time, then sour cream, vanilla, lemon zest and cornflour without overbeating.

stages.title: Bake gently
steps: Pour filling over crust and bake at 160°C until edges are set but centre still wobbles slightly.
Turn off oven and leave door ajar for 30 minutes to cool gradually.

stages.title: Chill before slicing
steps: Cool completely at room temperature, then refrigerate at least 6 hours.
Run a warm knife around edge before removing tin and slicing.

tips: Room-temperature ingredients reduce lumps and cracks.
variations: Top with a quick berry compote after chilling.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze individual slices up to 2 months.

title: Matcha shortbread
summary: Buttery shortbread biscuits with earthy matcha flavour and a delicate, crisp bite.
method: Beat the softened butter and icing sugar until smooth and pale, then mix in the egg yolk.
Sift the flour, matcha and salt together, then fold into the butter mixture until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into a 4 cm wide log, wrap tightly and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until firm enough to slice.
Cut the log into 7 mm rounds and arrange on lined trays.
Bake at 165°C until the edges are set but the biscuits are still green, then cool on the tray.

stages.title: Cream butter
steps: Beat butter and icing sugar until smooth and pale.
Mix in egg yolk until incorporated.

stages.title: Add dry ingredients
steps: Sift flour, matcha and salt together to remove lumps.
Fold into butter mixture just until a soft dough forms.

stages.title: Shape and chill
steps: Roll dough into a log about 4 cm wide and wrap tightly.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes until firm enough to slice neatly.

stages.title: Slice and bake
steps: Cut 7 mm rounds and arrange on lined trays.
Bake at 165°C until edges are set but biscuits remain green, then cool on tray.

tips: Use culinary-grade matcha and avoid overbaking, which dulls its colour.
variations: Dip half of each cooled biscuit in white chocolate.
storage: Airtight at room temperature up to 5 days; freeze dough up to 2 months.

title: Mango lassi
summary: Cool, creamy mango yoghurt drink with cardamom and a gentle tang.
method: Peel the mango and cut the flesh from the stone. Chill it first if you like a colder drink.
Blend the mango, yoghurt, milk, honey and cardamom until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste for sweetness, adding a splash more milk if it's too thick. Blend briefly with the ice cubes until frosty.
Pour into two glasses and serve immediately, dusted lightly with a little extra cardamom if you like.

stages.title: Prepare mango
steps: Peel mango and cut flesh away from the stone.
Chill fruit if possible for a colder drink.

stages.title: Blend ingredients
steps: Add mango, yoghurt, milk, honey and cardamom to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.

stages.title: Adjust consistency
steps: Taste for sweetness and add a splash more milk if too thick.
Blend briefly with ice cubes for a frosty texture.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Pour into two glasses and serve immediately.
Dust lightly with cardamom if desired.

tips: Very ripe mango needs less added honey.
variations: Use coconut yoghurt and oat milk for a dairy-free version.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 1 day; stir before serving.

title: Scallion pancakes
summary: Flaky, chewy scallion pancakes with crisp golden layers and a savoury spring onion filling.
method: Mix the flour and salt, stir in the hot water until shaggy, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into four balls and roll each into a thin circle. Brush with sesame oil and scatter over the spring onions.
Roll each circle into a tight log, coil it like a snail and tuck the end underneath. Rest briefly, then roll flat into rounds.
Fry in the neutral oil in a pan over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides.
Cut into wedges and serve with the soy sauce mixed with the rice vinegar.

stages.title: Make dough
steps: Mix flour and salt, then stir in hot water carefully until shaggy.
Knead until smooth, cover and rest for 20 minutes.

stages.title: Roll layers
steps: Divide dough into four balls and roll each into a thin circle.
Brush with sesame oil and scatter with spring onions.

stages.title: Coil and flatten
steps: Roll each circle into a tight log, coil like a snail and tuck the end underneath.
Rest briefly, then roll each coil into a flat round without pressing too hard.

stages.title: Pan-fry
steps: Fry in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides.
Cut into wedges and serve with soy sauce mixed with rice vinegar.

tips: Resting dough makes it easier to roll without springing back.
variations: Add a pinch of five-spice powder to the oil.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pancakes up to 3 days; re-crisp in pan.
